subject.title: [Feature]:  Expose claude-cli thinking blocks as reasoning on /v1/responses (and /v1/chat/completions)`

question: Should the Gateway expose real reasoning to HTTP clients, and if so should it be request-scoped opt-in with embedded text and Claude CLI progress represented as distinct output types?
rationale: This changes a public HTTP disclosure contract and must distinguish real text from upstream-withheld Claude CLI data; source inspection cannot choose the project’s privacy and compatibility policy.

options.title: Adopt an explicit opt-in HTTP contract
options.body: Define documented Responses and Chat Completions reasoning/progress events, default them off, and implement embedded-text projection plus truthful CLI progress.

options.title: Keep reasoning off HTTP
options.body: Retain chat and Control UI reasoning surfaces only, avoiding a new external disclosure contract.

options.title: Limit the first release to embedded reasoning
options.body: Ship a request-scoped embedded-runtime reasoning projection now and leave Claude CLI progress or text for a separately specified follow-up.

recommendation.title: Adopt an explicit opt-in HTTP contract
recommendation.body: Define documented Responses and Chat Completions reasoning/progress events, default them off, and implement embedded-text projection plus truthful CLI progress.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the closest current CLI reasoning boundary and documents how the existing privacy gates behave.
